messages:
maya: Heads-up — AtlasPay is hitting a bunch of 504s and long p95 tails from hosted. Support ticket: #AP-342. They say errors started ~10:00 UTC after a marketing push. I'm seeing influx + continuous-batcher backlog in the traces.
ryan: Paging @oncall-tim. Can you pull ingress queue depth & batcher backlog for tenant id atlaspay-prod?
ops-bot: Alert: hosted-gateway[us-west-2] - request_queue_depth > 90% for tenant atlaspay-prod (5m avg). Incident ID: I-20270315-279.
sarah: Repro steps from support: small repro curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b","prompt":"payroll calc ...","max_tokens":400}'` — their traffic is many concurrent long-seq requests (avg seq 1200).
maya: Logs show kvcache eviction spikes when backlog grows. snippet: ```batcher_queue_len=312 kv_evictions=27 served=0 p95=2.4s```
ryan: Sounds like continuous batching is accumulating long sequences and hitting per-tenant queue cap. Two quick mitigations: 1) enable tenant soft-limit to shed long requests to lower-priority pool, 2) temporarily route atlaspay-prod to smaller-quantized model to reduce per-token time.
support-jess: Customer wants minimal changes; they prefer rate-limiting over model change. Is there a quick rate-limit throttle we can flip?
oncall-tim: I can apply a short-term ingress rate cap (concurrency cap) for atlaspay-prod and enable fallback to the reserved burst pool. Doing it for next 15m while we root cause. Will post changelog.
ops-bot: Change applied: tenant_concurrency_cap=40 for atlaspay-prod by oncall-tim at 1795552705. Fallback pool enabled.
sarah: After cap, p95 dropped from ~2.4s -> 0.8s and 504s trend down. Still seeing backlog spikes at ~minute marks when concurrent long seqs overlap.
maya: Root cause hypothesis: mix of many long-seq requests + continuous batcher not ageing old groups because of sticky grouping heuristics. Also kvcache misses force reencode overhead.
ryan: Two follow-ups: a) add a quick guard to batcher to cap per-tenant pending batch size (config flag), b) add telemetry to split long-seq traffic to dedicated longseq pool automatically. I'll file a PR.
support-jess: Customer asks for repro steps so they can avoid triggering. Can we give a minimal repro to illustrate the tail?
sarah: Minimal repro: spin 50 concurrent requests with seq length ~1200 with small inter-arrival jitter. Script: ```for i in $(seq 1 50); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b","prompt":"x","max_tokens":1200}' & done```
oncall-tim: Added runbook note: if per-tenant queue > 80% for 3m -> apply concurrency_cap and route to fallback. Marked in runbook v2. ops runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ingress-queue-shedding
maya: Filing support reply with mitigation steps and ETA for config change. Also adding customer to scheduled patch window for model routing tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
ryan: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523 — implements per-tenant pending-batch cap + telemetry. Tests added.
support-jess: Customer confirmed improvement after cap. Leaving ticket open for follow-up on longterm fix. :thumbsup:
maya: Closing the Slack thread when PR merges and runbook updated. Thanks all.
